The club competes in [[Major League Soccer]] (MLS) as a member of the [[Eastern Conference (MLS)|Eastern Conference]]. Since April 2026, Inter Miami plays home matches at [[Nu Stadium]], having played at the interim [[Chase Stadium]] prior. On January 29, 2018, MLS officially approved an [[expansion team]] in Miami.{{Cite news |date=January 29, 2018 |title=Miami MLS expansion team to begin play in 2020 |url=https://www.mlssoccer.com/post/2018/01/29/miami-mls-expansion-team-begin-play-2020 |access-date=March 28, 2019 |website=MLSSoccer.com |publisher=MLS Digital |archive-date=February 4, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210204011959/https://www.mlssoccer.com/post/2018/01/29/miami-mls-expansion-team-begin-play-2020 |url-status=live }}{{Cite web |date=January 29, 2018 |title=MLS announces David Beckham's expansion team in Miami |url=http://www.espn.com/soccer/major-league-soccer/story/3361118/mls-finally-announces-david-beckhams-expansion-team-in-miami |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=January 29, 2018 |archive-date=February 28, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180228134028/http://www.espn.com/soccer/major-league-soccer/story/3361118/mls-finally-announces-david-beckhams-expansion-team-in-miami |url-status=live }} The club garnered international attention prior to its founding because of co-owner [[David Beckham]], and again in 2023 with the signing of [[Lionel Messi]] on a free transfer. Since the team began playing in the [[2020 Major League Soccer season|2020 season]], it has signed several other high-profile players such as [[Blaise Matuidi]] and [[Gonzalo Higuaín]] in 2020, [[Sergio Busquets]], [[Jordi Alba]] in 2023, [[Luis Suárez]] in 2024, [[Rodrigo De Paul]] in 2025 and [[Sergio Reguilón]] and [[Casemiro]] in 2026. Following Messi's debut, the team won its first major trophy, the [[2023 Leagues Cup]], which also qualified the team to the [[2024 CONCACAF Champions Cup]] for the first time. In the [[2024 Major League Soccer season|2024 season]], Inter Miami secured its first [[Supporters' Shield]], which qualified the club to the [[2025 FIFA Club World Cup]] as hosts.{{Cite web |last=mlssoccer |title=Inter Miami win 2024 MLS Supporters' Shield |website=MLSSoccer.com |url=https://www.mlssoccer.com/news/inter-miami-win-2024-mls-supporters-shield |access-date=October 3, 2024 |archive-date=October 8, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241008032911/https://www.mlssoccer.com/news/inter-miami-win-2024-mls-supporters-shield |url-status=live }} The team's [[Forbes list of the most valuable MLS clubs|estimated value according to ''Forbes'']] is $1.2 billion {{as of|2025|lc=y}}, ranking second in the league behind [[Los Angeles FC]].
